content.text: {"summary":"The linear damping coefficient c is the negative slope of the output with respect to velocity v at the origin, because the quadratic drag term v|v| has zero slope there. At x=0 the active hidden units are 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 8, 9, 10 and 11. Summing W2[i]*W1[i][1] over those units gives a slope of about -0.747, so c is estimated at 0.747. This is approximate: the network's piecewise-linear fit of v|v| may put a small extra slope near zero. To double c, the two unused hidden units (0 and 7) are set up as ReLU(v) and ReLU(-v). They get output weights -c and +c, which together add exactly -c*v everywhere. No other parameters change, so the drag, restoring, force and bias terms are preserved.","estimated_c":0.747183,"patches":[{"tensor":"W1","index":[0,1],"value":1.0},{"tensor":"b1","index":[0],"value":0.0},{"tensor":"W2","index":[0],"value":-0.747183},{"tensor":"W1","index":[7,1],"value":-1.0},{"tensor":"b1","index":[7],"value":0.0},{"tensor":"W2","index":[7],"value":0.747183}]}
